# free forever — full entry text

## 1. freecode — Free forever

A coding agent on web, desktop and terminal. Sponsor cards pay the model bill.

- **URL:** https://freecode.sh/
- **Free:** Free access with a daily usage limit; the site says access resets and tells you when.
- **Paid by:** Sponsor cards are shown in the interface, clearly labelled, and the FAQ says they are “not written into your code”.
- **Runs on:** Web · Desktop (preview) · Terminal
- **Licence:** Not stated on the site; the CLI ships on npm as freecode-sh.
- **Why it is on this page:** One of only two here that runs in a browser as well as a terminal, with a start-up guide and an FAQ that names the trade-off instead of hiding it.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26
- **Top pick** on the page.

The catch:

- The npm installer covers Apple-silicon macOS and Windows x64 only — Intel Macs, Linux and Windows on ARM are out.
- Web use asks for GitHub read and write access to your repositories.
- The FAQ states session data feeds diagnostics, sponsored recommendations and “eligible data licensing”.

Sources:

- freecode: https://freecode.sh/
- freecode-faq: https://freecode.sh/faq
- freecode-getstarted: https://freecode.sh/guides/get-started

## 2. Freebuff — Free forever

The flagship ad-funded agent: CLI, desktop for every OS, browser, Android.

- **URL:** https://freebuff.com/
- **Free:** 30 hours a day on the free plan — but only in the vendor's 24 “full access” countries. Anywhere else it is 5 hours a day, and 4 over a VPN or proxy. One-hour sessions with unlimited messages; hours reset at midnight in your local timezone and do not roll over.
- **Paid by:** Text ads between agent turns. Paid tiers ($8 / $25 / $60) buy 50, 80 or 130 hours a day and unlock the better models.
- **Runs on:** Terminal · Desktop (macOS, Windows, Linux incl. ARM) · Web · Android
- **Licence:** Apache-2.0 (the free build of Codebuff).
- **Why it is on this page:** The widest platform coverage of anything ad-funded — Linux ARM builds and a phone app — and the only one publishing a plain hours table per model.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26
- **Top pick** on the page.

The catch:

- The 30 hours is regional. Full access covers the US, Canada, UK, Australia, NZ, Ireland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Finland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Austria, Germany, France, Spain, Italy, Portugal, Switzerland, Malta and South Korea; everywhere else the free allowance is 5 hours a day, or 4 on a VPN.
- Free runs the two DeepSeek V4.1 Flash variants (15 hrs/day, or 10 on Flash Fast) plus Solar Pro 4 and Solar Mini 4, and Beam 1.0, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and Glyph Cluster, which use none of your hours. GPT-6 Luna, Muse Spark 1.3, Muse Ember, Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Terra are paid-tier models.
- The launch post states messages, agent traces, files and usage may be analysed to personalise ads and train ad models.
- Hours, not tokens: an hour on a 3x model costs three of your hours.
- Full model list differs by country.

Sources:

- freebuff: https://freebuff.com/
- freebuff-pricing: https://freebuff.com/pricing
- freebuff-launch: https://freebuff.com/blog/freebuff-launch

## 3. free-pi — Free forever

Ad-funded terminal agent with 27 models, including opt-in “Defense” models that will not refuse.

- **URL:** https://freepi.ai/
- **Free:** A daily allowance set by the server — the limits docs deliberately do not state a number. /usage shows a percentage; a warning appears at 80%.
- **Paid by:** Terminal ad cards; /support opens today's advertiser. An ad partner receives excerpts of your recent conversation to pick the ad.
- **Runs on:** Terminal
- **Licence:** CLI is MIT.
- **Why it is on this page:** Listing this with its own consent text quoted, because that text is the clearest statement of the trade anywhere on this page. Also the only one with a bundled security-audit skill.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- The consent screen says it plainly: sessions are saved as traces and used to train models, and “they may be shared or sold to third parties” — with no opt-out after accepting.
- Alpha, no uptime guarantee, no self-service data deletion.
- One active session at a time per account.
- Every strong model costs a multiple of the allowance: Kimi K3.1 Pro ~22x, Gemini 4 Neon ~29x, GPT-6.2 Astra ~51x. The Claude and GPT-6.1 models are listed as “temporarily unavailable” right now.

Sources:

- freepi: https://freepi.ai/
- freepi-privacy: https://freepi.ai/docs/ads-and-privacy
- freepi-limits: https://freepi.ai/docs/models-and-limits

## 4. Tenzy — Free forever

Terminal agent built around showing its reasoning, its patches and its test proof.

- **URL:** https://tenzy.net/
- **Free:** Fair-use budget of 20h 35m of agent time per cycle, resetting every 15 hours. No card to install.
- **Paid by:** Sponsor banners rotate about every 15 seconds; between-turn placements appear after completed work with frequency caps.
- **Runs on:** Terminal
- **Licence:** Not stated on the site.
- **Why it is on this page:** Publishes the exact allowance (20:35:00, 15-hour reset) and an ad policy that rules out autoplay, fake download buttons and ads touching generated code.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-06

The catch:

- Ads are frequent by design: a rotating banner every ~15 seconds while one is visible.
- Agent-time accounting, not tokens — cheaper models stretch it, but the clock runs while the agent works.
- Default model is DeepSeek V4 Flash; NVIDIA Inkling needs your own key.
- The installer shown on the site is PowerShell-first.

Sources:

- tenzy: https://tenzy.net/
- tenzy-docs: https://tenzy.net/docs

## 5. VibeFree — Free forever

Free AI chat with no login, and the same deal inside a VS Code agent.

- **URL:** https://vibefree.dev/
- **Free:** Guest chat needs no account — an advert pays for each message. An account adds a free daily token allowance and VibeBucks.
- **Paid by:** One ad auction fills every slot; labelled sponsored units appear while the assistant works and beside its replies.
- **Runs on:** Web chat · VS Code extension · Android
- **Licence:** Proprietary extension (vibefree.vibefree-vscode). Trading name of TapTapPay Ltd.
- **Why it is on this page:** The only entry here you can use without creating anything, and it documents its ad classifier down to the character count.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- The ad classifier reads the first 1,500 characters of each message you send and keeps topic labels for 30 minutes. The message itself is not kept for ads.
- The VS Code extension is a chat panel, not autocomplete.
- External ad networks can, with your consent, ask the model to mention a sponsor inside an answer.
- Windows desktop app, CLI and standalone IDE are still in development.

Sources:

- vibefree: https://vibefree.dev/
- vibefree-free: https://vibefree.dev/docs/free-ai-chat/
- vibefree-ads: https://vibefree.dev/docs/ad-privacy-and-your-chat/
- vibefree-dev: https://vibefree.dev/developers

## 6. ADCode — Free forever

An AI code editor that pays you: half of eligible ad revenue is credited to you.

- **URL:** https://adcode.bluethenics.com/
- **Free:** 140 AI credits a day across included models — roughly 20 agent steps a day, per their own comparison.
- **Paid by:** Sponsored cards. Half of eligible ad revenue is credited to your account; the other half funds the editor. Plans from $19/month raise the allowance.
- **Runs on:** Browser · Desktop (Windows, Linux)
- **Licence:** Open source under Apache-2.0.
- **Why it is on this page:** The only product here that shares revenue with the user instead of just waiving the bill — and it publishes the step count rather than saying “generous”.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- 20 agent steps a day is a taste, not a working day. Builder ($19) is 85, Pro ($39) is 175, Max ($149) is 661.
- Free included AI is one sponsor's models — Tagflow Code 27B and Tagflow Code Flash, sponsored by Tagflow. Heabsy and every other hosted model are pay-as-you-go from credits.
- Earnings depend on eligible views and advertiser demand; they are not a wage.
- No macOS desktop build yet; the browser version needs a verified account for included AI.

Sources:

- adcode: https://adcode.bluethenics.com/
- adcode-pricing: https://adcode.bluethenics.com/pricing
- adcode-online: https://adcode.bluethenics.com/online-ai-code-editor

## 7. Clixad — Free forever

Terminal agent with no key and no subscription; free models daily, credits from an offerwall.

- **URL:** https://clixad.io/
- **Free:** Seven models free every day up to 60,000 credits of usage per account, inside a daily budget shared by all users; Gemini 3.8 Flash joins them until 15 January 2027. The 25,000-credit signup bonus is gone.
- **Paid by:** Marked terminal ads in up to three places (60-character lines, booked by advertisers by the week) plus surveys and offers completed in a browser tab that convert to credits.
- **Runs on:** Terminal · Browser chat
- **Licence:** CLI on npm under Apache-2.0.
- **Why it is on this page:** Publishes the arithmetic of its own funding, including the parts that are unflattering. `CLIXAD_SPONSOR=0` turns the ads off.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- Past the daily limit you pay in credits. Most survey attempts end in a screenout that pays nothing — Clixad's own blog says so.
- The free seven are not all budget models — GPT-5 Nano, GPT-6 Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5, GLM 5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and Kimi K2.5 — but everything above them needs earned or bought credits.
- Clixad's own funding post says free credits changed after it was written: the signup bonus its worked examples depend on is no longer issued.
- Public beta, 18+, shared daily budget so peak hours bite.
- The ad network still sees your IP; ad text is chosen by fixed category, never from prompts.

Sources:

- clixad: https://clixad.io/
- clixad-funded: https://clixad.io/blog/how-clixad-is-funded/

## 8. Idlen — Free forever

Not an agent — an extension that pays you for the time your AI spends thinking.

- **URL:** https://www.idlen.io/
- **Free:** $0 to install. You keep 70% of the ad revenue the wait earns, paid via Stripe, PayPal or as credits.
- **Paid by:** A native sponsored ad shown while the model is working. Advertisers reach you; you take 70% of that revenue.
- **Runs on:** VS Code / Cursor / Windsurf · Chrome · Firefox
- **Licence:** Extension code published for security review.
- **Why it is on this page:** A different question from the rest of this page: not “make AI free” but “let the wait pay for some of it”. Worth knowing it exists.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- It earns you money; it does not provide a model. You still bring Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or whatever you already pay for.
- Ad relevance is chosen locally from your package.json — the extension says it never reads source code.
- Their own earnings calculator (“€20–100/month”) is based on average fill rates, not a promise.
- A third-party extension inside your editor — review the code before installing.

Sources:

- idlen: https://www.idlen.io/

## 9. idlepay — Free forever

Swaps the “thinking…” spinner for one sponsored line. You keep half.

- **URL:** https://www.idlepay.co/
- **Free:** Free to install, no card, 50% revenue share, cash out via Stripe past $10.
- **Paid by:** One labelled sponsored line (≤60 characters) replaces the spinner verb during a genuine wait. Clicks pay 50× an impression.
- **Runs on:** VS Code · Cursor · Claude Code · Codex
- **Licence:** Open-source client, signed marketplace builds, verify.sh against public source.
- **Why it is on this page:** The most aggressively minimal version of the idea — one line, only during a real wait, verifiable builds.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- Same as Idlen: it monetises your wait, it does not give you a model.
- It reads one timestamp from your Claude session file to tell “coding” from “terminal left open”; everything else stays local.
- Uninstall restores your editor settings byte-for-byte — worth verifying yourself, since it does patch your Claude Code config.
- Earnings are estimates and depend on live bid prices.

Sources:

- idlepay: https://www.idlepay.co/

## 10. Overbrilliant OB-1 — Free forever

Open Apache-2.0 terminal agent with no account, no card and no key.

- **URL:** https://github.com/Overbrilliant/ob-1
- **Free:** A built-in free-models router — the project documents 150+ free models across 20+ providers — starts with no key or account; new free models reach free users after 30 days.
- **Paid by:** Vendor-funded free router; paid hosted tier is hard-capped prepaid credits with no overage path.
- **Runs on:** Terminal (macOS, Linux)
- **Licence:** Apache-2.0 CLI.
- **Why it is on this page:** The only entry that needs no account and no key at all, and its README says what the free router actually draws on instead of promising a model tier.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- overbrilliant.com no longer documents the agent at all: the site now sells custom-trained models from $1,500. The free CLI lives on GitHub and npm (@overbrilliant/ob1), with an Apache-2.0 licence and its own README.
- New free models lag 30 days behind paying users.
- The free router's capacity is whatever the keyless providers choose to give it, so throughput moves around.
- Sandboxing is macOS Seatbelt and Linux bubblewrap only.

Sources:

- ob1: https://overbrilliant.com/
- ob1-github: https://github.com/Overbrilliant/ob-1

## 11. opencode — Free forever

Open-source agent; its own gateway serves a rotating set of models at zero.

- **URL:** https://opencode.ai/
- **Free:** Free-tier chat models, usable inside OpenCode with no key or card.
- **Paid by:** The OpenCode Console gateway absorbs the cost; paid models and a Go subscription sit beside it.
- **Runs on:** Terminal · Desktop · IDE
- **Licence:** Open source.
- **Why it is on this page:** The most-installed open agent, with free models wired in rather than bolted on.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- The docs state free-tier chat models require OpenCode — you cannot call them from another client.
- The free list rotates with provider pricing.
- Console sign-in is needed for billing even though the CLI itself runs without an account.
- Free models are open-weight, never frontier.

Sources:

- opencode: https://opencode.ai/
- opencode-zen: https://opencode.ai/docs/zen/

## 12. Google Antigravity — Free forever

Agent-first IDE and CLI on a $0 individual plan — with real Claude and Gemini models.

- **URL:** https://antigravity.google/
- **Free:** $0 plan serving gemini-3.8-flash, claude-opus-4.6, claude-sonnet-4.6 and gpt-oss-120b — all four listed “until 2026-11-30”.
- **Paid by:** Google-funded. No ads at all. Gemini CLI's individual free tier ended 18 June 2026 and Google routes free users here.
- **Runs on:** IDE · CLI
- **Licence:** Proprietary.
- **Why it is on this page:** The strongest free models on this page without watching an ad. Listed as directory-verified because the plan details come from a probed directory, not a page I read.
- **Evidence:** probed directory · read 2026-11-26
- **Top pick** on the page.

The catch:

- Google account required, and Google can change the quota with one announcement — the directory that probes these rows already dates all four models “until 2026-11-30”.
- Gemini models and third-party models have separate weekly allowances, and neither amount is published.
- Gemini CLI's free tier being switched off is the cautionary tale: vendor free tiers are revocable.
- Proprietary and closed source.

Sources:

- antigravity: https://antigravity.google/
- awesome: https://mvalentsev.github.io/awesome-free-ai-coding/

## 13. Ollama (local models) — Free forever

The only genuinely free-of-strings option: your hardware, your models, no account.

- **URL:** https://ollama.com/
- **Free:** Download, pull a model, run it. No key, no account, no card, no telemetry to a vendor.
- **Paid by:** You pay in electricity and hardware. That is the whole business model.
- **Runs on:** Local runtime · Any OpenAI-compatible agent
- **Licence:** MIT (Ollama); model licences vary.
- **Why it is on this page:** Included because every other entry has an asterisk and this one does not. It is the baseline the rest are being measured against.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- Needs a machine with enough memory — a 27B coding model wants a real GPU, not a Chromebook.
- Quality is below frontier models; you are trading capability for independence.
- You still need an agent front-end (opencode, Cline, Continue, OB-1) pointed at localhost:11434.

Sources:

- ollama: https://ollama.com/
- ob1-github: https://github.com/Overbrilliant/ob-1

## 14. Kilo Code — Limited free

Open-source agent for VS Code, JetBrains and the CLI with an Auto Free mode.

- **URL:** https://kilo.ai/pricing
- **Free:** An Auto Free mode plus a keyless OpenAI-compatible gateway on a handful of free open models.
- **Paid by:** Free models are absorbed by the gateway; 500+ paid models bill through at provider rates.
- **Runs on:** VS Code · JetBrains · CLI
- **Licence:** Open source.
- **Why it is on this page:** Here rather than in the free-forever tier because the free path is a rotating pool, not a standing arrangement.
- **Evidence:** probed directory · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- Auto Free is deliberately the weaker path — mid-size open weights only.
- The gateway's free list rotates and can shrink without notice.
- One click on a paid model starts billing; easy to drift.

Sources:

- kilo: https://kilo.ai/pricing
- awesome: https://mvalentsev.github.io/awesome-free-ai-coding/

## 15. Kiro — Limited free

AWS's spec-driven agentic IDE with a perpetual free tier.

- **URL:** https://kiro.dev/
- **Free:** A perpetual free tier on Claude Sonnet and open-weight models — 50 credits a month, non-rolling, on requests served from the US; successor to Amazon Q Developer.
- **Paid by:** AWS-funded, no ads.
- **Runs on:** IDE · CLI
- **Licence:** Proprietary.
- **Why it is on this page:** Perpetual rather than promotional, which is why it is not in the “free forever” tier only because the quota is small.
- **Evidence:** probed directory · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- The workflow is opinionated: write requirements before code.
- AWS account required.
- The free quota is enough to evaluate, not to work in all day.

Sources:

- kiro: https://kiro.dev/
- awesome: https://mvalentsev.github.io/awesome-free-ai-coding/

## 16. Google Jules — Limited free

Async cloud agent: hand it a GitHub task and come back to a diff.

- **URL:** https://jules.google/
- **Free:** 15 async tasks per rolling day, 3 at a time, on Gemini models.
- **Paid by:** Google-funded.
- **Runs on:** Web
- **Licence:** Proprietary.
- **Why it is on this page:** Good for offloading chores, but the daily cap puts it in this tier.
- **Evidence:** probed directory · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- Asynchronous only — no real-time steering.
- GitHub connection required, with the repository access that implies.
- Small daily task count.

Sources:

- jules: https://jules.google/
- awesome: https://mvalentsev.github.io/awesome-free-ai-coding/

## 17. Duck.ai — Limited free

Private front-end to six free models with no account at all.

- **URL:** https://duck.ai/
- **Free:** Six models signed out: GPT-6 Luna, GPT-5.4 mini, Claude 4.5 Haiku, Mistral Small 4, gpt-oss-120b, Gemma 4 31B.
- **Paid by:** Funded by DuckDuckGo's search business. No ads in the chat.
- **Runs on:** Web
- **Licence:** Proprietary.
- **Why it is on this page:** No account and no ads, but an undisclosed cap — the honest description is “limited”.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- The daily limit is unpublished, and the big models burn it faster.
- Chat only — no files, no repository context.
- Chats stay on your device, so nothing follows you between machines.

Sources:

- duck: https://duck.ai/

## 18. Autohand Code — Limited free

Open-source agent for CLI, IDE, browser and mobile with a documented free plan.

- **URL:** https://docs.autohand.ai/getting-started/plans-and-pricing/free
- **Free:** 15 credits per rolling 5-hour window, up to 100 a month — one credit is one successful hosted response.
- **Paid by:** Hosted Fantail model is vendor-funded; BYOK and local models use no credits at all.
- **Runs on:** CLI · VS Code · JetBrains · Desktop · Mobile
- **Licence:** Open-source CLI.
- **Why it is on this page:** Publishes the full rate-limit matrix on a docs page — rare — but 100 responses a month is a trial in all but name.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- 100 hosted responses a month is roughly three a day.
- No card needed, but eligibility is verified: usually a GitHub account at least 30 days old.
- The free tier is Fantail only; other models mean your own key.

Sources:

- autohand: https://docs.autohand.ai/getting-started/plans-and-pricing/free

## 19. WorkBuddy — Limited free

IDE and CLI agent with a credit-based free plan and a heavy promotional period.

- **URL:** https://www.workbuddy.ai/docs/workbuddy/pricing
- **Free:** 100 credits a month, 5,000 code completions a month, 3 automated tasks — plus a limited-time promo of 30 credits a day.
- **Paid by:** Vendor-funded free plan; Pro at $10/month ($7 first month) buys 2,000 credits and unlimited completions.
- **Runs on:** IDE · CLI
- **Licence:** Proprietary.
- **Why it is on this page:** Listed because its docs separate base credits from promo credits — most products blur the two.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- The good numbers are promotional and the docs say plainly they will not always be available.
- 100 base credits a month is almost nothing once the promo ends.
- Credits are monthly and do not roll over.

Sources:

- workbuddy: https://www.workbuddy.ai/docs/workbuddy/pricing

## 20. DeepAI — Limited free

Free plan for chat, images and its DeepAI Code desktop app. API is paid.

- **URL:** https://deepai.org/pricing
- **Free:** Limited HD images and editing, limited standard chat, up to 250 “Theos” a day in DeepAI Code, 60s/day of voice chat.
- **Paid by:** Vendor-funded free tier with an ad-supported free experience; Pro at $9.99/month (or $7.50 annual) removes ads and raises everything.
- **Runs on:** Web chat · DeepAI Code desktop app · Website builder
- **Licence:** Proprietary.
- **Why it is on this page:** Worth including to kill a common assumption: DeepAI's free tier does not extend to its API, which its own docs say is Pro-only.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- Free chat is limited to Standard models. Genius and Super Genius — GPT-6.2 Sol, Grok 4.3, Claude Fable 5.2, Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.2 Astra, Gemini 4 Argon — are Pro only.
- The API is not free at all: the docs state API access requires a DeepAI Pro subscription.
- Theos are a daily allowance, not a durable pool.

Sources:

- deepai: https://deepai.org/pricing
- deepai-docs: https://deepai.org/docs

## 21. Cursor (Hobby) — Limited free

The best-known AI editor; its free plan is small and clearly a funnel.

- **URL:** https://cursor.com/pricing
- **Free:** A limited free allotment of agent requests and completions on the Hobby plan.
- **Paid by:** Subscription from $20/month; the free plan is product-led acquisition.
- **Runs on:** Desktop editor
- **Licence:** Proprietary.
- **Why it is on this page:** Included as a calibration point: this is what the industry calls “a free plan” when the aim is conversion.
- **Evidence:** probed directory · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- The free quota lasts a short session, not a week of work.
- The best models are behind the paid plans.
- Account required.

Sources:

- cursor: https://cursor.com/pricing
- awesome: https://mvalentsev.github.io/awesome-free-ai-coding/

The catch:

- The allowance is one-time, not monthly.

## 24. GitHub Copilot Free — Limited free

The default free plan most people already have by accident.

- **URL:** https://github.com/features/copilot
- **Free:** A free individual plan: 2,000 completions a month plus a chat and agent allowance GitHub does not put a number on.
- **Paid by:** Vendor-funded free tier; paid plans from $10.
- **Runs on:** VS Code · JetBrains · Visual Studio · CLI
- **Licence:** Proprietary.
- **Why it is on this page:** Usually already available to you, which makes it the free tier most people should try before installing anything else.
- **Evidence:** probed directory · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- Monthly completions and chat requests run out quickly once an agent is involved.
- Free sign-ups have been paused and reopened at various points — availability has changed before.
- GitHub account required.

Sources:

- copilot: https://github.com/features/copilot
- awesome: https://mvalentsev.github.io/awesome-free-ai-coding/

## 25. Codex (ChatGPT Free) — Limited free

Codex access on a $0 ChatGPT plan, where the rollout allows it.

- **URL:** https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing
- **Free:** Codex on the Free plan, subject to rollout; unlimited text chat with GPT-6 Luna.
- **Paid by:** Vendor-funded; Plus at $20/month.
- **Runs on:** Desktop · Web · CLI
- **Licence:** Proprietary.
- **Why it is on this page:** Genuinely usable for small tasks, but “unpublished allowance” is the whole problem with vendor free tiers.
- **Evidence:** probed directory · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- The free allowance is not published — OpenAI does not state a number.
- Rollout varies by country and account.
- ChatGPT account required.

Sources:

- codex: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing
- awesome: https://mvalentsev.github.io/awesome-free-ai-coding/

## 26. Macaly — Limited free

Chat-to-website builder with a real free plan: one published app, 1M credits a month.

- **Free:** 1 published app on a Macaly domain, 1M monthly credits, limited usage through ChatGPT and Claude.
- **Paid by:** Vendor-funded free plan; Starter $10/month unlocks custom domains.

The catch:

- One published app only, and no custom domain until you pay.
- Monthly credits, not a daily drip.

## 29. Groq — Limited free

## 31. OpenRouter — Limited free

One key for a rotating set of zero-priced models, plus a free router.

- **URL:** https://openrouter.ai/
- **Free:** Models priced at zero, and an `openrouter/free` router that picks one at random for each request.
- **Paid by:** Providers and paid traffic subsidise the free pool.
- **Runs on:** API
- **Licence:** Proprietary service, OpenAI-compatible.
- **Why it is on this page:** The single key that drops into nearly every agent here as BYOK, with no card.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- Free models are rate-limited and heavily used.
- Some free routes log prompts for training — read each model card.
- The free list rotates constantly; the router may pick a weaker model than you expected.

Sources:

## 32. FreeInference (Harvard SEAS) — Limited free

A university lab serving open models free, including an Anthropic-shaped endpoint.

- **URL:** https://freeinference.org/
- **Free:** Free open models — DeepSeek V4 Flash, GLM 5.3 Flash, MiniMax M3, Qwen 3.6 — over OpenAI and Anthropic-shaped endpoints.
- **Paid by:** University research project.
- **Runs on:** API
- **Licence:** Research service.
- **Why it is on this page:** The only free endpoint that speaks Anthropic's protocol, so existing Claude Code habits carry over.
- **Evidence:** probed directory · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- Research capacity: uptime is best-effort and it could stop without notice.
- The Anthropic-shaped endpoint slots into Claude Code but is not an officially supported pairing.
- Prompts and responses may be logged for research, and sanitised content and usage statistics may be published. It is a lab experiment, not a privacy product.
- Key required.

Sources:

- freeinference: https://freeinference.org/
- awesome: https://mvalentsev.github.io/awesome-free-ai-coding/

## 38. awesome-free-ai-coding — Reference

118 live free offers, probe-verified twice a week, with the evidence linked.

- **URL:** https://mvalentsev.github.io/awesome-free-ai-coding/
- **Free:** MIT licensed. No tracking, no ads, no affiliate links.
- **Paid by:** Volunteer project; GitHub Actions probe every row twice a week and archive offers after three failed probes.
- **Runs on:** Web · GitHub · Atom feed
- **Licence:** MIT.
- **Why it is on this page:** The best place to check whether a free tier still exists this week, because every row links its proof.
- **Evidence:** vendor page · read 2026-11-26
- **Top pick** on the page.

The catch:

- It is a list — you still wire everything up.
- Ended offers can linger until the next probe.
- Very broad: easy to disappear into.

Sources:

- awesome: https://mvalentsev.github.io/awesome-free-ai-coding/

## 42. Azure for Students — Reference

$100 of credit a year plus free services, no credit card.

- **URL:** https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students/
- **Free:** $100 credit per year, renewable while enrolled.
- **Paid by:** Microsoft-funded for full-time university students.
- **Runs on:** Cloud
- **Licence:** n/a
- **Why it is on this page:** Enough to host a real side project — and an AI endpoint — for a year without a card.
- **Evidence:** probed directory · read 2026-11-26

The catch:

- Full-time university students only, verified.
- Credit does not roll over, and overages stop services.
- Azure's pricing is not cheap.

Sources:

- azure: https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students/
